name: vwap_mean_reversion_5s_4
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks that deviate significantly from VWAP tend to revert because VWAP represents the fair institutional execution price. Large-cap stocks overshoot VWAP due to retail panic selling or momentum chasing, creating temporary dislocations. Institutional algorithms that benchmark to VWAP create a gravitational pull back toward it. This edge persists because retail traders lack the discipline to fade moves mechanically, and the required speed of execution discourages manual traders.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

indicators.name: vwap_zscore
indicators.purpose: measure deviation from VWAP in standardized units

exit.signal_exit: exit when vwap_zscore crosses 0 from the entry side

filters.volume_filter: skip if bar volume < 50% of SMA(volume, 20)
filters.expiry_filter: skip on F&O expiry day, skip on budget day

weaknesses: Fails in strong trending days where VWAP itself trends away — stocks can stay 2+ sigma for hours
VIX spikes above 20 destroy mean reversion; this filter reduces opportunity set significantly
Confirmation bar requirement adds slippage and sometimes misses the best entry by 5-10 bps
prior_art: Classic VWAP mean reversion — widely known, edge is in the specific z-score threshold and filters
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
